subject.title: fix: handle Claude CLI synthetic placeholders

question: Should a Claude CLI synthetic placeholder be treated as a terminal fallback result, or must resumed live sessions keep reading and preserve the same session because a real answer may arrive later?
rationale: Both behaviors are observed for the same upstream marker, and choosing terminal fallback changes message delivery, model routing, and persisted session ownership; source inspection alone cannot determine the intended product policy.

options.title: Require lifecycle-aware handling
options.body: Recognize the marker in parsing, but make resumed Claude sessions continue or preserve the process until a true terminal outcome is established.

options.title: Accept terminal fallback semantics
options.body: Treat every marker-only result as terminal and explicitly accept that some resumed sessions may rerun the prompt and abandon a later original answer.

recommendation.title: Require lifecycle-aware handling
recommendation.body: Recognize the marker in parsing, but make resumed Claude sessions continue or preserve the process until a true terminal outcome is established.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work directly owns resumed CLI lifecycle and timeout semantics, the closest boundary for this decision.
